An OpMode is the base class for every robot program in FTC.

It controls the lifecycle of your robot code: initialization, match start, the main loop, and finally stop.

Every program you write extends either OpMode or LinearOpMode.

LinearOpMode runs top-to-bottom on a single thread.

You call waitForStart() to wait for the start button, then use while(opModeIsActive()) to loop until the match ends.

Beginners find it easy because code flows like a recipe, but if any step gets stuck, the whole robot freezes.

OpMode has lifecycle methods that the SDK calls automatically: init() runs once when you press INIT, and loop() is called repeatedly after START.

Because each loop() call is non-blocking, you return quickly and let the SDK handle the next frame.

This fits the command scheduler model used in Module 2.

From this point forward, every lesson uses OpMode, not LinearOpMode.

OpMode avoids stuck-loop pitfalls because each loop() call must return.

It also works with the command scheduler you'll learn in Module 2, where commands submit work and the scheduler drives it each frame.

Knowing both models helps you understand why OpMode is the better foundation.
